summary: [Flaky] Filters BIPolicyIsApplied AzureAD tests intermittently failing (3 tests)
description:
## Problem

3 BIPolicyIsApplied AzureAD-related tests in PMfW Regression - Filters are intermittently failing on shared sets of nightly runs (period 2026-04-14 to 2026-04-29), strongly suggesting a shared root cause around AzureAD group filter evaluation. Tracked as rows #18-#20 in the flakey test epic [EPM-54749](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/browse/EPM-54749).

## Affected Tests

* BIPolicyIsAppliedBecauseUserMatchesAnAzureADGroupAndAWindowsGroup (10 failures, 10/20 = 50%)
* BIPolicyIsAppliedBecauseUserMatchesAllAzureADGroups (8 failures, 8/20 = 40%)
* BIPolicyIsAppliedBecauseUserMatchesAnAzureADGroup (8 failures, 8/20 = 40%)
* `BIPolicyIsNotAppliedBecauseUserDoesNotMatchAllAzureADGroups`
* `BIPolicyIsNotAppliedBecauseUserMatchesAnAzureADGroupButNotAWindowsGroup`

## Affected Runs

* [2026-04-14](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24415134496)
* [2026-04-16](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24486209007)
* [2026-04-21](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24698306838)
* [2026-04-22](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24754338446)
* [2026-04-23](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24810691324)
* [2026-04-28](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25028030370)
* [2026-04-28](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25081806786)
* [2026-04-29](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25085687687)

Classification: Automation. Concentrated on ARM64 (24H2 & 25H2) endpoints. Failure mode is a token-mismatch assertion when a DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe launch evaluates the AzureAD group filter against a not-yet-populated cache.

## Implementation

### Root cause

IdpGroupsBindings.PrivilegeManagementForWindowsAlreadyKnowsAboutMyUser (the binding for the Background step "Given Privilege Management for Windows already knows about my user" used by all BIAzureADFilters.feature scenarios) launches a warmup DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe to trigger PMfW's first-time AzureAD group fetch from the mock BeyondInsight service, then waits with a fixed Thread.Sleep(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3)). The fetch is asynchronous; on slower endpoints (every observed failure is on ARM64 - 11-24H2AF26-A05/A09, 11-25H2AF26-A02/A10) the fetch outruns the 3-second budget. When the test's "When I run 'DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe' ..." step then launches the dummy app, PMfW evaluates the AzureAD group filter against an empty cache, the rule doesn't match, no admin token is added, and the "Then the Administrator token is applied to 'DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe'" assertion fails after its 20-second accesschk retry loop. The original author's comment on the binding explicitly notes this race ("PMfW does not wait for the request to PMC to go through") but used a sleep instead of a poll.

### Fix

In Tests/Automation/BeyondTrust.Automation.Windows.Bindings.Common/IdpGroupsBindings.cs, replace Thread.Sleep(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3)) with a Polly-based wait that snapshots IdPGroupsCache.GetLastModifiedTime() before launching the warmup process and polls (30 retries x 1s) until the mtime advances after the kill - proving the service has flushed the AzureAD fetch result to %ProgramData%\\Avecto\\Privilege Guard\\AzureADCache\\<sid>\\. Mirrors the existing GroupsRefreshed binding (same file, lines 104-120) and reuses imports already present (Polly, IdPGroupsCache).

### Validation

Cherry-pick the fix onto a soak branch and run PMfW Regression - Filters on the ARM 24H2/25H2 endpoint pool at >=20 iterations targeting the affected BIAzureAD\* scenarios. Confirm pass rate >=99% (was 40-50%) and that the new poll exits well under 30 seconds in the steady-state case. Confirm no regression on x64 LTSC builds where the suite previously passed.

### Pull request

[#3815 - https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/pull/3815](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/pull/3815)

* [2026-05-04](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25296042132)
* [2026-05-05](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25352063141)

Classification: Automation. All 8 observed failures across 4 sampled nightly builds (2026-04-28 to 2026-05-05) hit Windows 11 24H2/25H2 ARM64 endpoints. No x64/x86 endpoint reproduced. The visible exception is NullReferenceException("Windows list was empty, or contained only nulls") thrown by DeferredActions.ClickAppButton when UIA3 returns no top-level windows for the spawned DeferredDummyApp.exe within FlaUI's 5-second default timeout.

## Implementation

### Root cause

DeferredActions.ClickAppButton (and AssertDummyOpenVisible) call Retry.WhileEmpty(() => app.GetAllTopLevelWindows(new UIA3Automation())) to discover the DeferredDummyApp top-level window. The call inherits the framework-wide FlaUI default timeout configured in CommonSetup.cs (Retry.DefaultTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(5000)). DeferredDummyApp.exe is a .NET Framework 4.8 x64 WinForms application; on Windows 11 ARM64 it runs under Microsoft's x64 emulation layer, which makes process startup and first-paint substantially slower than the 5s budget. When the timeout fires, WhileEmpty returns an empty array, the explicit windows == null || windows.All(i => i == null) check then throws NullReferenceException. 100% of failures across the sampled window are on ARM64 24H2/25H2 endpoints; no x64 endpoint has reproduced.

### Fix

In Tests/Automation/BeyondTrust.Automation.Windows.Framework/Helpers/DeferredActions.cs, pass an explicit 30s timeout: argument to the Retry.WhileEmpty calls in ClickAppButton and AssertDummyOpenVisible. Local override only - the global FlaUI 5s default is unchanged, so other waits (which already pass on ARM64) are unaffected. 30s comfortably exceeds the observed \~12s emulation startup envelope while keeping bounded failure semantics if the window genuinely never appears. Consistent with similar overrides already in the framework (e.g. NotificationPopup.cs:489 uses 60s for a WhileNull UI wait).

### Validation

Re-run PMfW Regression - Upgrading on the affected ARM64 machines plus a 5-iteration soak to confirm the flake is gone; spot-check a non-ARM64 run to confirm no regression. The 30s upper bound is consistent with similar timeout overrides already in the framework.

[#3813 - https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/pull/3813](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/pull/3813)

summary: Add missing [AfterTestRun] hooks to BeyondInsightIntegration, IdentityCore, and IdentityIntegration suites
description:
## Problem

`BeyondInsightIntegration`, `IdentityCore`, and `IdentityIntegration` have a `[BeforeTestRun]` hook calling `CommonSetup.TestRunSetup()` but no matching `[AfterTestRun]` hook, so `CommonTeardown.TestRunTeardown()` never runs. The teardown's `Directory.Delete` step for fixture dirs (`BatchFiles`, `Configs`, `Content`, `Installers`, `Resources`, `TestResultFiles`, `AutoTempDir`) is skipped, leaking `Configs`/`Content`/`Resources` (\~380 KB, \~15 files per machine) into the per-machine `Artefacts/` uploads on `\\fs01\ExecutionProduction\...` for these three suites — visibly absent for working suites like AgentProtection.

Noticed during code-coverage work (coverage adds gated start/stop calls inside the same setup/teardown methods, so the missing `[AfterTestRun]` is also why coverage data isn't captured for these suites), but the gap is pre-existing and has been silently leaking fixture dirs into result uploads.

## Solution

Add an `[AfterTestRun]` hook calling `CommonTeardown.TestRunTeardown()` to each suite's bindings:

* `Tests/Automation/BeyondTrust.Automation.Windows.BeyondInsightIntegration/Bindings/GlobalHooks.cs`
* `Tests/Automation/BeyondTrust.Automation.Windows.IdentityCore/Bindings/IdentityCore.TeardownBindings.cs`
* `Tests/Automation/BeyondTrust.Automation.Windows.IdentityIntegration/Bindings/...`

summary: [Flaky] AppControl_AllowExecution_Challenge_Once_AfterServiceRestart intermittently failing
description:
## Problem

Test `AppControl_AllowExecution_Challenge_Once_AfterServiceRestart` in suite PMfW Regression - AppControl is intermittently failing. It has failed 3/20 runs (15%) in the period 2026-03-13 to 2026-04-09. Tracked as row #31 in the flakey test epic EPM-53105. The test involves challenge-once behaviour persisting across a service restart; the flakiness may relate to timing or state cleanup after the restart.

## Failure Runs

* “Assert.Fail failed. Timed out waiting 1 minute for process“:

    * [2026-03-16 — PMfW Regression - AppControl](https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/_build/results?buildId=342088)
    * [2026-03-17 — PMfW Regression - AppControl](https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/_build/results?buildId=342218)
    
* Network issue on VM:

    * [2026-04-02 — PMfW Regression - AppControl](https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/_build/results?buildId=344162)
    

# Claude Investigation

Full Investigation:

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=8aad4aa4-76a6-4c0e-98ef-bb69a4c16f06&&collection=&height=null&occurrenceKey=null&width=null&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)Summary and Next Steps:

\`PGChallengeResponse.exe\` (AMD64 binary) timed out on an ARM64 machine due to x64 emulation overhead.  
  
The smoking gun is the driver log around PGChallengeResponse startup:

```
P6376  Loading xtajit64.dll           ← x64 JIT translation on ARM64
[1098ms gap]
P6376  Loading kernel32.dll
P6376  [APC queued for hook injection]
[~9 seconds total before hook loads]
P6376  Hook loaded into 6376          ← PGHook finally in, at 01:09:56
```

The 30-second test timeout was simply not long enough for PGChallengeResponse.exe to compute and send the OTP response on an ARM64 machine running it under emulation.

\## Fix

\`PGChallengeResponse.exe\` needs to be compiled as a native ARM64 binary (or ARM64EC) so it does not go through \`xtajit64.dll\`. The 9-second DLL injection delay and slow execution that follow are purely a consequence of emulation overhead.

summary: Add integration test project for PortalApi
description:
## Background

PortalApi is PM Cloud's primary backend API serving the Portal UI. It has an extensive unit test project (`CoreServices/Tests/PortalApi.Tests`) but no integration tests that exercise the full ASP.NET Core pipeline. This ticket introduces a `WebApplicationFactory<Startup>`-based integration test project following the pattern established by `EpmMcpService.IntegrationTests`.

PortalApi is a large service (24+ controllers) with many cross-cutting concerns — RBAC authorization via `ClaimRequirementFilter`, LaunchDarkly feature flags, Azure Key Vault, NATS, Azure Storage, and Microsoft Graph. The initial integration test project should establish the infrastructure and cover the highest-value baseline suites, with additional suites added incrementally.

## Goal

Create `CoreServices/Tests/PortalApi.IntegrationTests` as a dedicated integration test project.

## Project Setup

* New project: `CoreServices/Tests/PortalApi.IntegrationTests/PortalApi.IntegrationTests.csproj`
* Target framework: net9.0, `IsPackable: false`
* Key NuGet dependencies:

    * `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing`
    * `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`
    * `NUnit` (4.x)
    * `Moq`
    * `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.InMemory`, `.Sqlite`, `.SqlServer`
    * `Testcontainers.MsSql`
    * `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt`
    
* Project references: `PortalApi.csproj`, `TestHelpers.csproj`
* Add `settings.runsettings` with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = IntegrationTest`

## Base Class: `PortalApiIntegrationTestBase`

* `WebApplicationFactory<Startup> Factory`, `HttpClient Client`, `Guid TenantId`
* Database: SQLite in-memory by default; SQL Server via `TEST_DB_PROVIDER=SqlServer` env var; `SqlServerContainerFixture` for container lifecycle
* `[OneTimeSetUp]` / `[OneTimeTearDown]` / `[SetUp]` hooks with database cleanup between tests
* Mocked external dependencies:

    * Azure Key Vault (certificate provider + secret client)
    * NATS connection service
    * PlatformGatewayClient (cross-service HTTP client)
    * Microsoft Graph client
    * Azure Blob Storage client
    * LaunchDarkly (offline mode)
    
* `ConfigureTestAuthentication(services)` using `TestAuthHandler` — claims must be compatible with `ClaimRequirementFilter` (RBAC)
* `AuthorizeClient(Guid userId, PermissionsSeed permissions)` — mirrors EpmMcpService pattern
* Helper: `PortalRoute(string path)` — prepends the service's base path + version prefix

## Test Suites (Baseline — Initial Scope)

summary: test: AppControl_ChallengeANDAuth_RunAsCurrentUser flaky on ARM64 — UI automation failures
description:
## Problem

The test `AppControl_ChallengeANDAuth_RunAsCurrentUser` is flaky, primarily on ARM64 machines. It failed across 4 regression runs between 2026-03-16 and 2026-03-25 with three distinct failure modes, all rooted in FlaUI UI automation issues interacting with the EPM challenge/authentication notification dialog.

Failing runs:

* 2026-03-16 — **PMfW Regression - AppControlAuth** (Build 342088) — [https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/\_build/results?buildId=342088](https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/_build/results?buildId=342088)
* 2026-03-17 — **PMfW Regression - AppControlAuth** (Build 342218) — [https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/\_build/results?buildId=342218](https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/_build/results?buildId=342218)
* 2026-03-25 — **PMfW Regression - AppControlAuth** (Build 343184) — [https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/\_build/results?buildId=343184](https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/_build/results?buildId=343184)

## Failure Modes

### 1. "Failed to fill In EditBox" (Build 343184, 11-25H2-A-13 — Win 11 25H2 ARM64)

* 42/63 tests failed on this machine
* Password step succeeded (popup was visible and functional), challenge code retrieved correctly
* FillInEditBoxWithContent("Response code", ...) failed after 10 retries (22.4s)
* Root cause: `Keyboard.Type()` sends keystrokes to the focused window, not the specific control. `PGChallengeResponse.exe` launched with `UseShellExecute = true` spawns a visible window that steals focus.

### 2. "Timed out waiting 1 minute for process" (Builds 342088 & 342218, ARM64 machines)

* Affected machines: 11-25H2-A-14 (Win 11 25H2 ARM64), 11-24H2-A-12 (Win 11 24H2 ARM64)
* Dialog interaction steps appeared to complete, but DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe never started within the 1-minute timeout
* Suggests the "Authorize" button click didn't register properly, or the authorisation response wasn't sent back to the service

### 3. NullReferenceException in FillInPassword (Build 342218, B-2016-08 — Windows 2016)

* 45/63 tests failed on this machine — a machine-level problem
* `Window.FindFirstDescendant(cf => cf.ByAutomationId("1017"))` returned null, causing NRE inside the Polly retry loop
* Machine is a quarantine candidate

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the **PMfW Regression - AppControlAuth** suite against ARM64 endpoints (Windows 11 24H2/25H2 ARM64). The test is intermittently flaky — not every run fails, but ARM64 machines are consistently affected.

## Expected Behaviour

The test should reliably enter the challenge response code into the notification popup edit box and the authorised process should start on all platforms including ARM64.

## Actual Behaviour

On ARM64 machines, the test fails with multiple error modes: edit box interaction fails (focus stolen by PGChallengeResponse.exe window), process start times out, or NullReferenceException when UI elements are not found.

## Recommendations

1. **Use SetValuePattern instead of Keyboard.Type()** in `FillInEditBoxWithContent` (NotificationPopup.cs:130) — write directly to the control via UIA, bypassing focus issues. The current click-selectall-type approach is inherently fragile.
2. **Remove UseShellExecute = true** from the PGChallengeResponse.exe runner in `EnterAResponseCodeIntoThePopupFromTheCmdLine` (DefendPointNotificationBindings.cs:99-102) — the exit code (response code) is all that's needed; no GUI interaction is required. Running without shell execute avoids spawning a focus-stealing window.
3. **Add null-check in FillInPassword** (NotificationPopup.cs:201-202) — `FindFirstDescendant(...).AsTextBox()` can return null if the password field is not found. Adding a null check with a meaningful error message would make failures more diagnosable rather than producing a bare NullReferenceException.
4. **Quarantine B-2016-08 and 11-25H2-A-13** — both had mass failure rates (45/63 and 42/63 respectively), indicating machine-level problems beyond individual test flakiness.

summary: Race condition in TheProcessHasStarted causes flaky AllowExecution_ShellExecuteRunAsAdmin_Commandline_BAT
description:
AI Fix: bs/epm-52397/fix-flaky-race-condition-the-process-has-started

## Problem

The `TheProcessHasStarted` binding in `RunProcessBindings.cs` calls `Process.GetProcessById(process.Id)` to create a new Process instance (to survive the `using` block disposing the original). However, fast-exiting processes like `ShellExecApplication.exe` can exit before this call executes, causing an `ArgumentException` ("Process with an Id of X is not running").

`ShellExecApplication.exe` calls Win32 `ShellExecute("runas", ...)` which is fire-and-forget — the process exits immediately after ShellExecute returns. For BAT files specifically, the Windows shell handler resolves quickly, making this variant most susceptible to the race.

The UAC enablement for the EventAuditLegacy suite (commit `801f9bf62`, merged 2026-03-18) changed the process launch path to use `NativeProcessApi.LaunchNativeProcess` on UAC machines, which altered timing characteristics and increased the failure rate.

## Steps to Reproduce

* Run the `PMfW Regression - EventAuditLegacy` suite
* Observe the `AllowExecution_ShellExecuteRunAsAdmin_Commandline_BAT` test — it fails intermittently
* Failed on builds: 340931 (2026-03-04), 342492 (2026-03-19), 342659 (2026-03-20)

## Expected Behaviour

The `"the process has started"` step should succeed regardless of how quickly the launched process exits, since it only needs to verify the process was created — not that it is still running.

## Actual Behaviour

`Process.GetProcessById(process.Id)` throws `ArgumentException` when ShellExecApplication.exe has already exited, causing the test to fail with an unhandled exception. This is a timing-dependent race condition — more likely on fast machines or with fast file types (BAT).

  Scenario: BI - JSON - Content Control - Add Admin - 600  
  	When I open the content file 'add-admin.txt' from 'DeployDirectory' with the DummyContentHandler  
  	Then the DummyContentHandler was 'allowed to access' the file  
  	And '1' 'BI' JSON events are created, one of which includes the following details:  
  		| EventID | Description         | ContentFileName | ApplicationGroup | Token                                    |  
  		| 600     | DummyContentHandler | add-admin.txt   | Add Admin Rights | Add Full Admin (Required for Installers) |

# The point at which the test failed

* Feature setup (CreateEventsFolder) — Directory.Delete throws IOException: "The process cannot access the file 'dummyfile15144' because it is being used by another process"
* The file C:\\ProgramData\\Avecto\\Privilege Guard\\BeyondInsight Events\\dummyfile15144 is locked by testhost.x86.exe

# Why do you think it failed?

* The preceding scenario "BI - JSON not created if event folder is full" (@EPM-17603, @BIEventFolderFull) calls File.Create() 25,000 times in EventLogsBindings.cs (TheEventsFolderIsFull) without disposing the returned FileStream:

```
// EventLogsBindings.cs ~line 1395
SysIO.File.Create(path + "\\dummyfile" + i);  // FileStream returned but never disposed
```

* This leaves up to 25,000 open file handles held by testhost.x86.exe. When the next scenario's BeforeScenario calls CreateEventsFolder, Directory.Delete cannot remove the locked files and throws IOException.
* Fix: wrap in a using to ensure immediate disposal: using (SysIO.File.Create(path + "\\dummyfile" + i)) { }
* Cascade effect: the dirty events folder also causes all subsequent tests in @UseFakeBIAdapter-tagged features to fail. BeforeFeature calls CreateFakeAdapter which also calls DeleteEventsFolder — when that throws, AddService is never reached so the fake BeyondInsight adapter service is never registered. AfterFeature then calls RemoveFakeAdapter → RemoveService → fails with "service does not exist" → Assert.Fail is thrown before DeleteEventsFolder can clean up, leaving the folder permanently dirty and cascading through all remaining features in the run.

summary: [Flaky] Compatibility PGHookLoadedWhenDefault* tests intermittently failing (3 tests)
description:
## Problem

3 tests in PMfW Regression - Compatibility failed on the same single nightly run (2026-04-20) - same date, same suite, strongly suggesting a shared root cause. Each failed 16 times (16/20). Tracked as rows #3-#5 in the flakey test epic [EPM-54749](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/browse/EPM-54749).

## Affected Tests

* PGHookLoadedWhenDefaultIsAPCAndProcessIsInOverrideList_UsesIDT (16 failures)
* PGHookLoadedWhenDefaultIsIDTAndProcessIsInOverrideList_UsesAPC (16 failures)
* PGHookLoadedWhenDefaultIsIDTAndProcessIsNOTInOverrideList_UsesIDT (16 failures)

## Affected Runs

* [2026-04-20](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24643511667)

Classification: Environmental (already-corrected pipeline pinning, no further code change needed). All three tests failed on a single bad night and have not failed since.

## Implementation

### Root cause

The 2026-04-20 nightly Compatibility run (build 24643511667, build number 26.2.1.219) was the first scheduled run after PR [#3292](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/pull/3292) ("feat: Make hook injection method fallback list bidirectional \[EPM-24503\]", commit [5d32846c9](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/commit/5d32846c9)) merged on 2026-04-17. That PR added three new scenarios to InjectReliability.feature plus the new DRIVER_INFOV(L"Using %s injection because process is in override list") and "Using %s injection due to HookLoadMethod" trace strings in PGDriver/DllInjectionManager.cpp::SelectInjectionMethod.

However, the driver-build pipeline failed counter-signing on the feature commit (run 16) and on every subsequent attempt until run 22 on 2026-04-20 20:41 UTC. Throughout that window DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER in .github/workflows/build.yml was pinned to 13 (the last successful pre-feature run, sha 1befabcbcb, 04-15). The 04-20 nightly therefore deployed the new client + new test code against the old driver, which did not contain the override logic or emit the expected trace strings. The captured ETL log on every failing machine shows the driver took the legacy "Using APC injection due to HookLoadMethod" branch instead of the new "because process is in override list" branch. The pattern matched zero times in 30s of retries -> assertion fail x 3 tests x 16 machines = the 48 deterministic failures. This is a feature/driver-pin staleness: any nightly that deploys with a pre-feature DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER will reliably fail these three scenarios.

### Fix

No code fix - recommend closing as environmental. PR [#3739](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/pull/3739) ("chore: update driver pin to run 22 \[EPM-51801\]", commit [a402feb65](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/commit/a402feb65), 2026-04-21) already corrected DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER: 13 -> 22 in .github/workflows/build.yml. Run 22 was the first successful driver build containing the bidirectional override feature.

### Validation

Verified the three tests pass on every Compatibility nightly run since the pin update (build IDs sampled: 25028030370 04-28, 24971630723 04-27, 25085687687 04-29, 25197279777 05-01, 25296042132 05-04, 25352063141 05-05). Each run shows Compatibility passed=1694 failed=0 with zero PGHookLoadedWhenDefault\* failures. Window covers all 16 supported OSes including ARM64 24H2/25H2. No further action required.

summary: Add integration test project for AdConnectorService
description:
## Background

AdConnectorService currently has a unit test project (`CoreServices/Tests/AdConnectorService.Tests`) but no integration tests that exercise the full ASP.NET Core request pipeline. This ticket introduces a new integration test project following the pattern established by `EpmMcpService.IntegrationTests`.

## Goal

Create `CoreServices/Tests/AdConnectorService.IntegrationTests` with a `WebApplicationFactory<Startup>`-based test base and initial test suites covering authorization, data contracts, sorting, filtering, pagination, and feature flag behavior testing, where applicable.

## Project Setup

* New project: `CoreServices/Tests/AdConnectorService.IntegrationTests/AdConnectorService.IntegrationTests.csproj`
* Target framework: net9.0, `IsPackable: false`
* Key NuGet dependencies (mirror EpmMcpService.IntegrationTests):

    * `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing`
    * `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`
    * `NUnit` (4.x)
    * `Moq`
    * `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.InMemory`, `.Sqlite`, `.SqlServer`
    * `Testcontainers.MsSql`
    * `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt`
    
* Project references: `AdConnectorService.csproj`, `TestHelpers.csproj`
* Add `settings.runsettings` with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = IntegrationTest`

## Base Class: `AdConnectorIntegrationTestBase`

Mirror the structure of `McpIntegrationTestBase`:

* `WebApplicationFactory<Startup> Factory`, `HttpClient Client`, `Guid TenantId`
* Database: SQLite in-memory by default; SQL Server via `TEST_DB_PROVIDER=SqlServer` env var; `SqlServerContainerFixture` for container lifecycle
* `[OneTimeSetUp]` / `[OneTimeTearDown]` / `[SetUp]` hooks with database cleanup between tests
* Mocked external dependencies: Azure Key Vault (certificate provider + secret client), NATS connection service, LaunchDarkly (offline mode)
* `ConfigureTestAuthentication(services)` using `TestAuthHandler` — must support both auth schemes used by this service (see Notes)
* Helper: `AdConnectorRoute(string path)` — prepends the service's base path + version prefix

## Notes

* AdConnectorService uses **two distinct auth schemes**: `AgentScheme` (machine-to-machine, for the AD Connector agent) and `JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme` (for Portal-originated requests via `SearchController`). The `TestAuthHandler` registration and token generation must support both.
* Filtering/sorting test suites are **not applicable** — this service does not expose paginated list endpoints with sort/filter query parameters in the EpmMcpService style.
* The `ActivationController`, `DiscoveryController`, and `CallbackController` auth requirements should be confirmed during implementation; scope additional authorization test cases accordingly.

summary: Automation: Pathfinder login flow
description:
**Technical problem**: When a user logs in, we need to “clear old groups/permissions” and “insert new groups/permissions”.  Without a transaction, other concurrent requests can read the database in the tiny window after the DELETE but before the INSERT and see the user as having no permission groups.   
To fix this error, we added a transaction to the database, but EF doesn’t support transactions with Core’s execution strategy, which caused a bug for newly created instances.  
We can’t access the actual DB, so it is not possible to write a unit test for this code. 

**Business logic:** When logging into a Pathfinder instance, whether new or upgraded, it’s important to make sure the correct PMC token is generated. This helps prevent 401 errors and ensures users can access the PMC based on their RBAC permissions. A code change in the EPM YARP proxy is needed to fix this issue.

**Test Goal:** Verify that a concurrent request reading a user's permission groups during a login operation (which clears and reinserts those groups) never observes the user as having zero groups.

**Setup**

* Use WebApplicationFactory for the YARP proxy service
* Replace the database with SQLite in-memory (same pattern as MCP integration tests)
* Seed: a user record, their existing permission groups, and the group memberships that should survive the login cycle

**Test steps**

1. Fire two tasks concurrently using Task.WhenAll:  
  \- Task A: POST to the login endpoint for the seeded user, which triggers the clear-old-groups + insert-new-groups path  
  \- Task B: immediately after Task A starts, GET an endpoint that reads the user's group membership from the database
2. Repeat the concurrent pair in a loop (10–20 iterations) to increase the probability of hitting the race window: a single execution may not be sufficient to expose a race condition reliably

**Assertions**

* Task B must never return a response consistent with the user having no groups (e.g. a 401 or an empty group list)
* After Task A completes, query the database directly and assert the correct groups are present: not zero, not duplicates

  Additional case - new instance compatibility

* Seed a user with no prior group records (simulates a newly created instance where there is nothing to delete)
* Call login
* Assert the insert succeeds and the correct groups are present in the database
* This covers the execution strategy bug where the transaction failed on new instances that had no rows to delete

**Notes for implementation**

* The race condition requires the test to genuinely interleave database operations, which SQLite in-memory supports since it runs in-process, no need for a real SQL Server instance
* If the login path uses EF Core's retry execution strategy, the test setup will need to either disable retries or configure a strategy that supports user-initiated transactions, since the fix being tested  
  relies on that transaction working correctly
* The loop repetition approach is a pragmatic alternative to injecting a deliberate delay into the production code path, which should not be done just to make a test deterministic
